description: Independently curated synthetic engineering scenarios. Requirements are predeclared in fixture, NEVER passed into retrieval. They test context sufficiency proxies, not actual AI task success.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 6 and Charters 01/03 define selection versus intended scope; Charter 14 section 6 owns correction, preview, and mutation authorization; Charter 15 covers verification.
cases.task: Implement Contextual Command for selecting one file and requesting that all files in its parent folder be moved to a destination. Handle the correction 'only the highlighted file', preview bulk effects, and obtain approval before filesystem mutation.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution sections 5 and 17, Charter 02 motion and accessibility sections, Charter 13 graphics resource budgets, and Charter 15 visual/performance acceptance govern the effect.
cases.task: Implement Atmospheric Motion particle effects with the Motion Coordinator; render GPU particles efficiently and automatically reduce graphic load during gaming without losing usability or reduced-motion accessibility.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 8 and Charter 04 connected-branch sections require separate histories and sourced sharing; Charter 08 governs retrieval; Charter 14 constrains private data access.
cases.task: Implement Connected Branches so sibling chats can find new post-fork findings, preserve provenance and selectively adopt knowledge, without leaking private project data or permissions.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 10 and Charter 08 compaction sections require recoverable source history and protected constraints; Charter 14 limits access; Charter 15 requires meaningful evaluation.
cases.task: Implement CIE adaptive compaction of long chat histories, preserving canonical messages, important user decisions and blockers, and checking protected constraints before continuing. Benchmark the quality and token tradeoff.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 9 and Charter 07 quick-capture sections require immediate durable capture; Charter 01 owns the interaction; Charter 08 owns later retrieval and Charter 14 privacy.
cases.task: Implement Quick Capture notes so a user can jot down an idea immediately without choosing a project or waiting for an AI response; classify the note asynchronously after saving it.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 11 and Charter 05 task/agent sections distinguish execution from completion; Charter 14 limits delegated authority; Charter 15 requires outcome evidence.
cases.task: Implement orchestration of specialized parallel agents working in isolated Git worktrees with task dependencies, safe delegation and evidence-based completion; never mark an unfinished task completed from a chat message.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 13 and Charter 09 evidence-class sections define observed, reported, and inferred activity; Charter 02 owns meaningful motion and Charter 14 prevents false privileged/audit claims.
cases.task: Implement a live Intelligence Stream with actual tool execution events and reasoning summaries. Show observed versus reported versus inferred evidence and never fabricate private internal thoughts.

cases.sourceReview: Constitution section 14 and Charter 10 accounting sections distinguish measured and estimated usage; Charter 08 governs context optimization and Charter 15 verification.
cases.task: Implement per-chat detailed token usage profiling for input output cached reasoning tokens, ensure accurate accounting and do not claim unmeasured savings from context compaction.
Keep one item pinned on two canvases; closing one tile must leave the original and its history intact.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 03 sections 1, 2 and 4 distinguish canonical resource, block instance, membership, and deletion; Charter 14 section 3 rejects display-name identity.

cases.task: Resume an agent assignment with another model provider after the first worker disconnects, carrying verified evidence and unresolved decisions without claiming identical hidden context.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 05 section on handoffs requires durable sourced checkpoints; Charter 12 sections on backend contracts and recovery prohibit false equivalence; Charter 14 bounds transferred authority.

cases.task: Forward a provider-initiated approval request for a terminal command, then reconcile a cancelled or disconnected response before any retry.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 12 approval protocol and retry sections require request identity and confirmed decision delivery; Charter 14 requires action-bound authorization and honest execution states.

cases.task: Vela opens the item the user called 'this' from the active selection and changes its workspace membership while keeping source ownership and permissions clear.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 06 requires a structured context envelope and grounded referents; Charter 03 owns resource identity and membership; Charter 14 controls authorization.

cases.task: Save a workspace layout and resource membership across restart and schema migration while two windows may edit the same object.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 03 persistence and recovery section requires durable identity, migration and concurrent update handling; Charter 14 governs protected data lifecycle.

cases.task: Ingest a noisy stream from a worker, preserve real source and ordering, and keep approval failures visible even when storage or rendering falls behind.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 09 event identity, pipeline, backpressure and storage sections require traceable source and critical-event priority; Charter 14 controls audit integrity.

cases.task: Animate a resource moving into a detached window after its layout is saved; the object must remain the same and keyboard users must still operate it with reduced motion.
cases.sourceReview: Charter 02 owns motion and reduced-motion behavior; Charter 03 owns persistent identity and layout recovery; Charter 13 owns display performance; Charter 14 includes accessible authorization where action scope changes.
